chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from al-Yasa', from Abu 'Abdillah (AS), and from 'Abd al-Wahid ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Ja'far (AS) — both of them said:
There is no divorce except for the one who intended the divorce.

key_terms.أَرَادَ: Arada — intended/willed; the requirement of genuine volitional intent as a condition for the validity of a legal act
key_terms.طَلَاق: Talaq — the Islamic institution of divorce initiated by the husband, requiring specific verbal formula and intention under Shia jurisprudence
key_terms.لَا ... إِلَّا: La ... illa — the absolute negation-exception formula meaning 'there is no X except Y', used in legal maxims to establish conditions

ai.seo_question: Is divorce valid if not intended in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a foundational legal ruling on Islamic divorce, transmitted through two parallel chains leading to both Imam al-Sadiq and Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon them). The ruling establishes that divorce (talaq) is legally invalid unless the husband genuinely intends it — a principle guarding against coerced, accidental, or frivolous pronouncements. In the early Islamic community, disputes over whether emotionally spoken words constituted binding divorce were common, and this ruling clarified that sincere intention (niyyah) is an indispensable condition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, from Al Yas’a, from Abu Abdullahasws, and from Abdul Wahid Bin Al Mukhtar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws, both of themasws having said: ‘
There is no divorce except for the one who intended the divorce’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah from al-Yasa’ from abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, from ‘ Abd al-Wahid ibn al-Mukhtar from abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja‘far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not a divorce unless it is intended to be a divorce.’”
